name: Teachers, Prophets and Reformers of the World's Faiths
description: From Mahavira and the Buddha to the Reformation and the leaders of today, the religious figures who founded, renewed or reshaped great traditions.

checkpoints.name: The first prophets
checkpoints.note: Abraham, honoured by Jews, Christians and Muslims, and Moses, who gave the law in Jewish tradition, are known mainly from sacred texts, and Zoroaster's dates are disputed and may lie well before 600 BCE. Their stories shaped three of the world's faiths.

checkpoints.name: The age of teachers
checkpoints.note: In India and China, Mahavira, the Buddha, Confucius and, by tradition, Laozi teach ways of living that shape huge parts of Asia. Their dates are traditional, and their words were written down by followers.

checkpoints.name: New faiths spread
checkpoints.note: Jesus's teaching is carried round the Mediterranean by Paul, and Muhammad founds a community in Arabia. Ali's leadership leads to the lasting split between Sunni and Shia Muslims.

checkpoints.name: Mystics, monks and masters
checkpoints.note: Kūkai, Shankara, Hildegard, Francis, Rumi and Nichiren teach in monasteries and on the road, each giving their tradition a new voice in Japan, India, Germany, Italy and Anatolia.

checkpoints.name: The Great Reformers
checkpoints.note: Guru Nanak founds Sikhism, and Luther's challenge to Rome in 1517 begins the Reformation. Calvin builds a new church, while Ignatius renews the Catholic one.

checkpoints.name: Faith in the modern world
checkpoints.note: Wesley, Joseph Smith, Mother Teresa and the Dalai Lama show religion at work in preaching, new movements, charity and exile.
